claims.explanation: Didanosine is a nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor that also inhibits mitochondrial DNA polymerase gamma and is activated by purine nucleoside phosphorylase (PNP); selectivity likely reflects dependence on purine salvage/PNP-mediated activation and on mitochondrial DNA polymerase gamma for survival, so lines with high PNP expression and low mitochondrial reserve are most sensitive. TP53 loss and PI3K/PTEN pathway activation may further lower the apoptotic threshold or increase metabolic demand, enhancing didanosine toxicity.

features.basis: PNP activates didanosine by phosphorolysis; high expression increases active metabolite
TP53 mutation/loss is enriched in selectively killed lines and impairs DNA damage response
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT, increasing metabolic and mitochondrial dependence
PIK3CA mutation is common in sensitive lines and may increase mitochondrial metabolism
Higher mitochondrial DNA polymerase gamma expression may buffer didanosine-induced mtDNA depletion
BRAF mutation appears in several sensitive melanoma/colorectal lines and may alter metabolism
KRAS mutation is present in sensitive pancreatic/colorectal lines and increases metabolic demand
ATM loss may impair repair of didanosine-induced DNA damage
CDKN2A loss is common in sensitive lines and may deregulate cell cycle checkpoints
NF1 mutation activates RAS/MAPK and may increase metabolic stress
STK11 loss is present in sensitive lines and may impair metabolic stress responses
SMARCA4 mutation appears in resistant lines and may reduce dependence on oxidative metabolism
